hints.title: Pair Search and Temporal Direction Obstacle
hints.text: Checking all possible buy and sell day pairs takes quadratic time. As you move forward in time, what single quantity from past days is sufficient to evaluate the profit of selling today?

hints.title: Running Minimum Purchase Price
hints.text: To maximize profit on day i, you should buy at the lowest price seen prior to day i. Maintaining a running minimum price allows instant evaluation of potential profit at each step.

hints.title: Single-Pass Min and Profit Update
hints.text: Track min_price initialized to infinity and max_profit initialized to 0. For each price, update min_price with the minimum of itself and the current price, then update max_profit with the maximum of itself and (current price - min_price).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of prices array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single forward pass with constant extra memory tracking minimum price and maximum profit.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all pairs (i, j) where i < j takes O(N^2) time. For N = 10^5, N^2 / 2 = 5 * 10^9 operations, exceeding the time limit.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Single-pass running minimum uses O(1) space and achieves O(N) linear time, avoiding any extra data structures.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Immediate identification of the one-pass invariant, handling monotonically decreasing prices (returning 0 profit), and O(1) auxiliary space.
